title: 14 Years in Power, Lost to a List With No Leader #Shorts
description:
Serbia: 14 years in power, and it may be over. On Sunday, October 25th, Serbia, a country of under seven million people, held a snap election, and the Student List, born from student protests, appears to have won more than half the vote in the partial count. It named no prime minister candidate, like a team winning the league without a captain. A majority needs 126 of 250 seats. Turnout was nearly 70 percent, reportedly the highest in over 30 years. Who becomes prime minister is still open. Results are not final.

Images: Wikimedia Commons (CC, credited on screen) and Pixabay stock; some clips are illustrative, not of the event.

Made by AI. Made with hope.
Subscribe for the day's news explained in a minute.
